It carries it four separate ways with the correct pin, classifies my advisory as operative under D-057 clause 3, and cites the D-039 precedent for the form. It also arrives with every element the D-078 cycle had to be told to add — the D-054 path, the revocation sentence, the strengthened MF-6 limb 'under its own reviewed act' — present from the outset. All seven digests verify, including the rider's own; all seven commits resolve; all seven cited decisions are ADOPTED.

The header states the entry owner-records DR-009 'as v2 plus rider RB-DR009-V2-A1'; the disposition pin carries '**plus operative rider RB-DR009-V2-A1** (D-076)' with the applied head's path and digest inline; the advisory-classification block names it; and clause 1 records the disposition 'plus rider RB-DR009-V2-A1' as the owner-recorded disposition.

So this entry inherits the rider rather than re-deriving or paraphrasing it.

It reads 'Claude 2 RBDR009V2-C2-A1 is **operative**. It is carried as rider RB-DR009-V2-A1 (same form as D-039 / RB-DR005-V2-A1). Codex had no advisory. The rider does not close LN-13, derivationDigest, R1-PARK-*, or CIR-B1.' The D-039 precedent is real: that entry carries RB-DR005-V2-A1 in the same 'v2 plus this rider' construction.

Both are present from the outset: 'D-054 path docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-054.user-amendment.md sha256 c274d140… commit 29670ed…', and 'Compound. Overturn: C-D079, plus reconciliation of any later MF-6 note under its own reviewed act. Revoking or overturning D-054, D-057, or D-072 requires superseding this owner record.' That is the strengthened form D-078 only reached at turn 2, correctly re-targeted to D-072 as this row's selection.

I ran D-057 clause 3's pin list element by element: all fourteen are present — the dependency declaration with its revocation sentence, the D-054 path with sha256 and commit, the D-057 commit, the Route B selection D-072 commit, the coordinator recording D-076 commit, the pin correction D-080 commit, the disposition path with sha256, both verdict paths with sha256, the owner role, the preview scope, the advisory classification, the operative rider, the attributed Route A remainder, and the MF-6 reversal limb.

The entry explains it — 'one-locus pin correction of D-074's Codex verdict digest; D-076 inherits that pin' — which is accurate: D-076 carries no verdict digest of its own and inherits D-074's through the 'Same turn-1 verdicts as D-074' cross-reference, a structure I verified during the D-080 cycle.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED' fails: the header refuses SATISFIED, clause 2 scopes any effect to 'architecture-preview scope only', clause 3 states 'Does not mark DR-009 SATISFIED. The Route A remainder above stays owed', and the readiness effect reads 'Zero SATISFIED. Conditions 2–5 unchanged.' file 08's DR-009 status cell still leads HARD-BLOCKED.

The attacks 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' and 'file 08 edited' fail: the header refuses the implementation directory, clause 3 preserves condition 5 as the only implementation authorization, clause 4 refuses the file 08 edit under MF-6 and defers a cell note as a separate act, file 08 measures unchanged at its cited digest, and git reports zero changes under docs/v2/architecture.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. DR-009 is the row with the most to drop, because it is the only one carrying an operative rider, and the rider is the one my own advisory produced — so I could check both that it survived and that it survived unaltered. It is carried in four places, its pin matches live bytes, and it matches adopted D-076's path and digest rather than being re-derived. The advisory classification names my finding as operative and cites the D-039 precedent for the form, which is D-057 clause 3 applied rather than recited. What I also want on the record is that this entry arrives with the D-054 path, the revocation sentence and the strengthened MF-6 limb already in place — the three things D-078 had to be told to add one cycle earlier. The family absorbed that, rather than needing to be told a second time.
